newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon ups penalties for stealing from utilities.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon ups penalties for stealing from utilities.

text.p: The Lebanese parliament on Wednesday raised the penalty for filching from the state electricity, water and telephone utilities to three years in jail.

In an official drive to halt widespread filching, parliament approved a government bill raising penalties from two years in jail and a 500,000 Lebanese pounds ($323) fine to three years jail and one million pounds.
Many Lebanese illegally plugged into the state water, power and telephone networks during the 1975-90 civil war and still enjoy free amenities at heavy cost to the cash-strapped utilities.
Authorities even complain of difficulties in collecting payment from legal subscribers. The electricity ministry said in December it managed to collect only 40 percent of bills due in 1996.
Acting finance minister Fouad Siniora, who is under pressure to reduce massive budget deficits, complained in February that electricity bills were not being paid in wide areas of the country.
"Some politicians and senior officials are not paying. Do you believe that?" Siniora said.
